articleTitle: DNCP: A Robust Artificial Intelligence Based Alzheimer's Disease Detection Methodology by Using Deep Neural Classification Principle
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative disorder that causes cognitive decline, memory loss, and ultimately death. Early and accurate detection of AD is crucial for timely intervention and improving patient outcomes. This study proposes DNCP: a robust deep learning (DL) based classification methodology for AD detection. The model integrates advanced preprocessing techniques, such as image registration, intensity normalization, and noise reduction, to enhance the quality of neuroimaging data. A multimodal learning approach is utilized to combine features from specific brain regions of interest (ROI), including the hippocampus, gray matter, and white matter. Comparative analysis was conducted against state-of-the-art models such as CNNs (ResNet, VGG-16, AlexNet), RNNs, and AutoEncoders, demonstrating the superior performance of DNCP. The proposed model achieved an accuracy of 95.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, sensitivity of 94.1%, and specificity of 96.2%, outperforming all other models. The results show that the DNCP model provides an efficient and reliable solution for early-stage Alzheimer's detection, opening doors for enhanced diagnostic tools in clinical settings.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Internet of Things (IoT) Powered Railway Track Crack Detection Scheme Based on Smart Sensors Association
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This paper presents an IoT -powered railway track crack detection system that uses a combination of smart sensors and autonomous vehicles to detect cracks and obstacles in railway infrastructure. The system incorporates ultrasonic sensors, infrared (IR) sensors, and LED-LDR assemblies, enabling real-time monitoring and reporting of railway track conditions. Wireless communication protocols such as Wi- Fi, RF transmitters, and GPS are utilized to transmit data to central control systems. Through testing, the combined sensor setup demonstrated the highest crack detection accuracy of 98%, outperforming individual sensors with accuracies of 94 % for ultrasonic sensors, 90% for IR sensors, and 80% for LED-LDR. The system's response time averaged 460ms in the combined setup, with the LED-LDR setup being the slowest at 580ms. The system also showed resilience across varied environmental conditions, proving its robustness in both high and low temperature, humidity, and lighting scenarios. This efficient, solar-powered system reduces manual inspection efforts and ensures continuous, reliable operation. The proposed system offers an innovative, cost-effective solution to enhance railway safety and prevent potential accidents caused by track defects.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Assisted Crop Pest Classification Model by Using Enhanced Light Gradient Boost Machine (ELGBM) Logics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Many different kinds of pests and insects impede the development of vital field crops including wheat, sugarcane, and rice, and they also diminish agricultural yields. Due to their similar appearance in the early stages of crop growth, accurately classifying and identifying all varieties of crop insects is a challenging task for farmers. Automatic feature extraction and handling of complicated high-level features in image classification applications are two requirements for a new model that can solve this problem with the help of deep learning aided architectures. This study investigates the use of an Enhanced Light Gradient Boost Machine (ELGBM), a deep learning algorithm, for the purpose of crop pest classification and pesticide recommendation. The suggested model's efficacy is assessed by cross-validation with a traditional learning technique known as Convolution Neural Network (CNN). Furthermore, the system incorporates a recommendation component that proposes the most efficient pesticide options for crop protection depending on the discovered pests. The suggested methodology outperforms more traditional approaches in terms of classification accuracy, which is around 98%. The outcomes proved that the suggested ELGBM model outperformed pre-trained models in labeling different kinds of field crop insects, suggesting its potential for use in agricultural crop protection systems.

articleTitle: Brain Tumor Detection Using Hybrid Deep Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This study introduces a novel hybrid deep learning framework for automated brain tumor detection in MRI scans. The methodology combines convolutional neural networks (CNN) with long short-term memory (LSTM) networks to enhance the capture of spatial and sequential features. Additionally, advanced preprocessing techniques, such as wavelet transform and anisotropic diffusion filtering, improve data clarity, while Gabor filters and Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) are employed for texture and feature extraction. Leveraging pretrained EfficientNet models with transfer learning ensures high accuracy and efficiency. Deployed on a cloud-based system, this approach supports real-time clinical analysis, demonstrating potential for accurate and early diagnosis.

articleTitle: A Robust Crop Yield Forecasting Model Through Machine Learning Ensemble Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Accurate crop yield forecasting plays a vital role in effective agricultural management and resource planning. This study presents an advanced machine learning approach that utilizes comprehensive data and rigorous preprocessing to enhance model accuracy. A range of core regression techniques, including Random Forest Regressor (RFR), Gradient Boosting Regressor (GBR), XGBoost Regressor (XGBR), Decision Tree Regressor (DTR), CatBoost, and Extra Trees Regressor (ETR), were applied as foundational models for yield estimation. To further optimize predictions, ensemble methods such as Voting Regressor, Stacking Regressor, Bayesian Model Averaging (BMA), and Blending Ensemble were integrated, leveraging the strengths of individual models to achieve robust performance. This approach highlighted the effectiveness of ensemble frameworks in yield forecasting. The findings offer valuable insights for informed decision-making in agriculture, underscoring the methodology's potential for supporting policy development and improving predictive accuracy in agricultural management.

articleTitle: Integration of Motorized Bicycle for Sustainable Commuting
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Speed restrictions are common problems in electric bicycle drives. This problem makes these drives difficult to be used as an effective form of urban commuting. The ultimate goal of this project is to increase the speed capability by a noticeable margin. In order to do that, a Lithium Ferro phosphate (LiFePO4) battery has been implemented for better energy storage, long lasting life, and better power density. In conjunction with the battery, a motor controller is integrated to act as the brain of this bicycle system. Additionally, a BLDC hub motor has been incorporated because of its good torque and efficiency along with some additional safety features. This study pushes the envelope of smooth and sustainable commuting by improving bicycle technologies.

articleTitle: Predicting ADHD Subtypes Using Machine Learning on Brain Imaging Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The use of machine learning approaches to differentiate between various types of Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) using information from brain imaging. Our goal is to reduce the sensitivity of the ADHD subtype evaluation by using advanced neuroimaging technologies, such as structural and functional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), in combination with intelligent machine learning algorithms. Our methodology involves preprocessing brain MRI data, point birth, and training colored machine literacy models to categorize various forms of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). The performance of these models is assessed within the parameters of this study using attributes that are similar to recall, perfection, and delicacy. According to preliminary research, machine literacy may effectively distinguish between various forms of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), which offers a foundation for more precise and well-established therapeutic approaches. In addition to assisting people in realizing their greatest potential, this approach clarifies the brain processes underlying attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). Our results suggest that the individual procedure for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) could be rewritten by combining brain imaging data with machine literacy. This would lead to better clinical concerns and more tailored remedial actions.

articleTitle: Graph Data Science Application in Omni-Channel
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: In today's competitive retail environment, omni-channel e-commerce has become a critical strategy for delivering seamless customer experiences across diverse touchpoints such as websites, mobile apps, physical stores, and social media platforms. The complex relationships and interactions between customers, products, and channels present significant analytical challenges. Graph Data Science (GDS) offers a powerful framework to model and analyze these relationships, providing actionable insights to optimize customer engagement, detect fraud, and streamline supply chains. By representing entities such as customers and products as nodes, and their interactions as edges, GDS enables the use of advanced algorithms for community detection, link prediction, and anomaly detection. This paper explores the use of graph neural networks (GNNs) for tasks such as customer segmentation, personalized recommendations, and cross-channel journey optimization. Through real-world applications, the paper emphasizes how GDS transforms large-scale, unstructured e-commerce data into actionable insights, driving business growth and enhancing operational efficiency. This comprehensive analysis underscores the potential of GDS as an essential tool for retailers navigating the complexities of omni-channel commerce.

articleTitle: Feature Based Classification of Medical Images for Early Detection of Diseases
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Early condition detection is essential for efficient operation and treatment. This research article investigates a point-based bracket method for medical picture analysis to improve early complaint opinion's efficacy and subtlety. Key elements from medical pictures such as X-rays, MRIs, and CT scans are extracted by utilizing sophisticated image processing techniques. Additionally, machine literacy models trained on these attributes can classify the photographs into various complaint orders. Our methodology combines significant classifiers like support vector machines and neural networks with point birth ways like texture, form, and intensity-based styles. Empirical findings reveal that our methodology considerably enhances the delicacy of discovery for various ailments, such as neurological disorders, cardiovascular ailments, and cancer. The suggested approach provides a solid decision-support tool, which not only helps with early opinion but also lessens the workload for medical practitioners. Future research will focus on improving the system's functionality to include additional medical imaging modalities and incorporating it into clinical workflows.

Author Keywords: Techniques for feature extraction Healthcare machine learning

articleTitle: LTECP: Experimental Analysis of Medicinal Plant Recognition System Based on Learning Assisted Texture Evaluation and Classification Principle
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The experimental analysis of medicinal plant recognition systems based on the Learning-assisted Texture Evaluation and Classification Principle (LTECP) aimed to develop an efficient system for identifying medicinal plants using machine learning and deep learning models. The dataset consisted of multispectral and digital images of various medicinal plant leaves. Image preprocessing, feature extraction using texture and geometric features, and feature optimization through chisquare selection were integral parts of the system. Multiple classification models, including Random Forest, Support Vector Machines (SVM), and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), were tested. The CNN models, specifically InceptionV3, ResNet50, and VGG-16, significantly outperformed traditional machine learning models. The InceptionV3 architecture achieved the highest accuracy of 98.20%, while ResNet50 and VGG-16 reached accuracies of 97.00% and 96.50%, respectively. The best-performing models demonstrated high precision, recall, and F1-scores across different plant species, with minimal misclassification errors. Feature optimization improved model performance by focusing on the most relevant data points, increasing accuracy across all models by up to 5%. The results highlight the potential of CNN architectures for accurate medicinal plant recognition.

articleTitle: ONNS: Experimental Evaluation of Human Smile Recognition Based on Image Processing Assisted Optimized Neural Network Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This paper presents the experimental evaluation of human smile recognition using an image processing-assisted optimized neural network strategy (ONNS). The primary objective was to assess different neural network architectures and feature extraction techniques to improve the accuracy and real-time performance of smile detection. Several deep learning architectures, including a standard CNN, optimized CNN, BKNet, RetinaNet, and MobileNet, were evaluated on a smile recognition dataset. Geometric and texture-based feature extraction techniques such as Local Binary Patterns (LBP) and Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG) were employed to improve the robustness of the model. The results showed that the optimized CNN achieved the highest accuracy of 95.3%, with a precision of 93.6% and a recall of 94.1%. Furthermore, a real-time performance evaluation demonstrated that MobileNet, while achieving the fastest inference time of 10 ms (100 fps), had a slightly lower accuracy of 90.5%. The combination of geometric and texture features led to improved performance, with the combined method achieving an accuracy of 92%. These results indicate that the proposed optimized neural network strategy is effective in improving smile recognition accuracy while maintaining real-time performance.

articleTitle: Enhanced Multilingual Image Captioning: Integrating Text-to-Speech Translation and Sentiment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The aim of this project is to create a system that will improve the way we interact with text and images by using the capabilities of computer vision and natural language processing. The main purpose of using this system to generate human-readable image captions is to train a model that can accurately describe an image's contents. The project extends the functionality of the image captioning system by adding language translation inorder to give a multilingual support. The use of a few pre-trained models will enable users with varying language backgrounds use this system to acquire captions in different target languages. This involves integrating language translation techniques into the system and training different models for every target language. Further we extend the project by working in the field of sentiment analysis by identifying the sentiment (positive, negative, or neutral) of captions by examining text and images. For a better understanding of the emotional tone of the information, the system combines CNNs with natural language processing (NLP) algorithms for image analysis and text analysis.

articleTitle: Predictive Analytics for Parkinson's Disease Detection Leveraging Deep Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Parkinson disorder is a neurological disease that progresses gradually which is typified by the brain's dopamine-producing neurons becoming exhausted. This neuronal loss results by symptoms including tremors, muscle stiffness, bradykinesia, and balance difficulties. Early detection and accurate prediction of PD progression are especially crucial for improving management and intervention strategies. This study builds a prediction model with the use of MRI datasets. To detect Parkinson's disease from MRI data, this study uses deep learning algorithms, such as Inception, Xception, and VGG19, and evaluates how well they perform in terms of accuracy.

articleTitle: SNCS: Experimental Procedures to Develop Learning Based SMS Spam Identification Model by Using Superficial Neural Classification Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The increasing use of mobile communication has made SMS an essential medium for interaction, but it has also led to the rise of spam messages that pose significant security and privacy risks. This research proposes the development of an SMS spam identification model using a Superficial Neural Classification Strategy (SNCS), integrating both traditional machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) techniques. Datasets were preprocessed using tokenization, text cleaning, and word embedding, followed by feature extraction through Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF). Traditional ML models such as Naive Bayes and Support Vector Machines (SVM) were implemented alongside DL models like Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Gated Recurrent Units (GRU). The results demonstrated that DL models outperformed traditional models, with the CNN-LSTM achieving the highest accuracy at 95.12%, followed by LSTM at 94.55%. Traditional ML models also performed well, with Gradient Boosting achieving an accuracy of 90.12%. Furthermore, addressing the class imbalance in the dataset improved the model's performance significantly, enhancing recall and F1-scores across all models. This study highlights the importance of model selection and data balancing in improving spam detection accuracy.

articleTitle: Impact of Irradiation on NCFinFET at Different Incidence Angles Using Numerical Device Simulations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This study uses numerical device simulations to investigate the effect of irradiation on an MFIS NCFinFET structure. By analyzing the single event transient effect induced by ionizing particles with varying linear energy transfer values and different angles of incidence, we identify the specific regions of the device that are vulnerable to such interactions. The device's most vulnerable location is the one with the maximum Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">collect</inf>, while the least vulnerable site has the minimal Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">collect</inf>, Moreover, the vulnerable location of the device varies with the incidence angle.

articleTitle: Experimental Evaluation of IoT Powered Automated Wheel Chair Controlling Mechanism Based on Artificial Intelligence Principle
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This paper presents the experimental evaluation of an IoT-powered automated wheelchair control mechanism based on artificial intelligence (AI) principles. The system integrates smart features such as voice control, obstacle detection, and real-time health monitoring to improve mobility for individuals with disabilities. Key components include Arduino Nano and ESP8266 microcontrollers, 12V DC motors for movement, and various sensors for health monitoring and obstacle detection. The wheelchair can be controlled via smartphone using Bluetooth or Wi-Fi, and voice commands for hands-free operation. Results from the experiment show that the voice control system demonstrated an average recognition delay of 0.5 to 0.7 seconds, while total response times under load averaged around 1.3 seconds. Health monitoring sensors, including heart rate and temperature sensors, exhibited a high accuracy, with an error margin of less than 3% for heart rate and 0.5% for temperature measurements. Obstacle detection proved effective, with an average response time of 1.2 seconds for detecting objects at 50 cm distance. Overall, the system demonstrated reliable performance across different operational conditions, making it suitable for practical applications in healthcare and personal mobility. Future enhancements aim to integrate artificial intelligence for autonomous navigation and multilingual support in the voice recognition system.

articleTitle: Image Processing Based Automatic Traffic Control System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: As the number of people living in cities increases and more people drive, one of the most important problems is traffic congestion. An intelligent system that could effectively manage traffic congestion based on traffic density was required due to the rise in the number of cars. While current traffic management systems operate using fixed time-based methodologies, conventional traffic control systems are unable to manage the complicated traffic flow at junctions. There are numerous methods for establishing effective traffic control systems in urban areas. However, no method exists that is effective in real-time, and no system is prepared to accept changes on a constant basis. Using a digital image processing tool in MATLAB and the image processing technique known as morphological operations, the real-time traffic management system determines the percentage match to control the flow of traffic. By use MATLAB code that modifies the green, yellow, and red-light times in relation to traffic volume and density. To enhance its robustness and reliability the proposed traffic control system which is based on image processing also integrates advanced features such as scenarios involving emergency vehicles.

articleTitle: ENOL: A Robust Learning Based Methodology to Predict Mental Health Illness by Using Elevated Neural Optimization Logic
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The necessity for smart predictive tools to facilitate early diagnosis and intervention is emphasized by the rising incidence of mental health issues. This paper introduces Elevated Neural Optimization Logic (ENOL), that is intended to predict mental health illness by utilizing advanced neural network optimization techniques. To measure the efficiency of the proposed scheme, it is cross-validated with the conventional known as K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN). ENOL, to analyze complex patterns in mental health data, employs a deep learning framework optimized with complex optimization algorithms. ENOL employs deep architectures that improve optimization approaches, depending on the number of inputs among other things, to fine-tune the mental health condition by improving both precision and effectiveness in forecasting. The ENOL strategy predictive performance was significantly enhanced through experimental validation on a variety of datasets that encompassed a variety of mental health conditions. The effectiveness and newness as well were successful even for the model with 98% accuracy in the prediction. This level of accuracy shows the model is capable of accurately identifying prospective mental health problems and distinguishing between various conditions. The findings emphasize the potential level of ENOL is considered as an important tool for early mental health diagnosis, providing a data-driven strategy to comprehending and dealing with mental health challenges.

articleTitle: Leveraging Machine Learning to Detect Phishing Websites: Protecting Individuals and Businesses from Cyberattacks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Phishing attacks are one of the emergent threats in the cybersecurity domain as it involves malicious websites and emails focused on compromising the sensitive information of the victim. The research paper is focused on detecting the phishing URLs with the help of machine learning. The dataset contains more than 11,000 URLs; every URL is labeled as phishing or legitimate, with 89 features describing the URL, such as length, use of special characters, and domain details. The URLs are classified using ML models such as RF, SVC, and GBM. In this paper, a hybrid model is built by taking in an RF, an SVC, and a GBM, optimized using cross-validation and hyperparameter tuning. The efficiency of the models is grasped based on the evaluation metrics like precision, accuracy, recall, and F1-score. The hybrid model outperformed the individual algorithms with a detection accuracy of 95% on phishing URLs, thus indicating its ability to be used as an efficient phishing solution to enhance cybersecurity defenses.

articleTitle: Investigation & Development of Intelligent Controller to Navigate the Wheelchair Autonomous Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: In this paper, we give a self-sufficient situating and route framework for stair climbing robotic wheelchair. Right off the bat, the working standard and stair climbing robot in our research center are portrayed especially. Besides, the self-governing situating and route framework is exhibited. In this framework, we propose a strategy is essentially helpful for impaired people who are enduring from Parkinson's ailment or physically incapacitated or loss of motion patients. These kinds of people can't move on their own. They generally rely upon different people. This proposed strategy is exceptionally helpful to disabled people, without relying upon different people, so these people are unreservedly move with possessing bearings. The third component of our work is the GPS (Global Positioning System) module, which collects data from satellites and determines the position data before sending it to the client's PC (of Navigation framework) or observers(of Tracking framework) utilizing remote innovation (GSM). It has an additional arrangement of a joystick for incapacitated people who can without much of a stretch move his/her hand. Electronic framework setup, a sensor framework, a mechanical model, voice acknowledgment control and joystick control are considered. At long last, the trial result in the stair climbing robotized robot indicates the attainability of the self-governing situating and route.

articleTitle: Data Ownership and Control in IoT: Legal Rights and Responsibilities
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The purpose of this exploratory article is to investigate the complex geography of data power and control inside the Internet of Things (IoT) paradigm, with a particular emphasis on the legal rights and responsibilities of stakeholders. As a result of the development of Internet of Things bias, which generates huge quantities of data, the problems that surround power, access, and control have become substantially less complicated. This study elucidates the colourful bounds of data power and control by conducting a complete review of existing literature and legal structures. It takes into consideration the positions of device manufacturers, data collectors, and end-users. In a similar manner, it examines significant legal legislation and precedents, highlighting the difficulties and ambiguity that are associated with defining and administering data power rights. In addition, the study covers recently emerging issues such as data sovereignty and sequestration legislation, both of which have an additional impact on data governance in Internet of Things ecosystems. The purpose of this article is to provide clarity and assistance for governments, businesses, and individuals who are navigating the ever-changing landscape of data power and control in Internet of Things environments. This will be accomplished by outlining the legal geography and agitating implied counteraccusations.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Driven Alloy Property Analysis for Optimized Bio Medical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Within the context of the present era, biomaterials are of utmost importance. In recent decades, breakthroughs in medical and material processing fields have led to the development of numerous biomaterials with features that suits to wide variety of applications. The Biomaterials are mostly utilized in orthopaedic treatment, Odontology, delivering drugs, tissue engineering, and cardiac devices. A range of implant materials has been utilized throughout different fields of medical sciences that is based on the specific needs of each application. The Titanium based alloy combinations pulls many of the researcher's attention mainly because of its bio compatible properties that suits for various bio implantation applications. Hence, in this research paper, the Ti-Al-Nb-Mo alloy is considered and their properties are analysed using the machine learning based classifier and optimization can be done with the well-known efficient Particle-Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm. The suggested alloy is subjected to analyse the mechanical properties using the X-ray diffraction analysis (XRD) and Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) tests and then the model is trained with the Random Forest classifier that analyses the physical properties such as young's modulus and tensile strength of the proposed alloy with various ratios and then their features are optimized for better accuracy with proposed PSO. The results demonstrates that the proposed machine learning model with the integration of RF and PSO shows the better prediction accuracy of alloy properties that in turn reduces the complicated experimental testing and finds the suitable ratio of proposed alloy for the specific bio implant applications.

articleTitle: Design and Evaluation of Connectivity Based Home Automation System Based on Arduino
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: IoT encompasses interconnected devices that exchange data autonomously, enabling automation. Raspberry Pi, a compact computer, serves as an affordable platform for DIY projects, education, and IoT uses. The CHASA model integrates Arduino Nano and Arduino Mega modules to optimize energy efficiency in home automation networks. The model employs unidirectional communication and AES (Advanced Encryption Standard) encryption to minimize power consumption and enhance security. Experimentation evaluates the model's performance across key metrics, showcasing its superiority over existing protocols. Results reveal CHASA's higher packet delivery ratio, energy efficiency, lower data loss, routing overhead, and average delay. Comparative analysis demonstrates CHASA's effectiveness in enhancing IoT network performance and energy conservation.

articleTitle: Engineering Excellence Fabricating an Intelligent and Automated Railway Gate Control System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Providing automated railway gate operations at level crossings, as opposed to manually controlled gates, are the primary purpose of this planned effort. To prevent train accidents at unattended railway gates, the NodeMCU microcontroller was used to construct the suggested prototype model. Two reed sensors, one on each side of the gate, can detect whether a train is approaching the gate using this technology. When a train approaches or leaves a level crossing, reed sensors installed in front of the gate detect the train's arrival or departure, and geared DC motors controlled by a microcontroller open and close the gate, correspondingly. These results in a shorter period of time the gate is closed compared to manually controlled gates, which in turn minimizes the likelihood of human mistake. Using an infrared LED and an oscillator circuit, this study also suggests a method for detecting impediments between the gates when trains arrive. The use of metallic conductivity and a squire wave generating circuit for rail track cut detection is also included in this paper. This might help prevent significant railway accidents. We cross-validated the suggested model with regard to the standard Arduino based Railway Gate Control (ARGC) to evaluate its efficiency. The system is referred to as IoTRGCL.

articleTitle: DNCS: Artificial Intelligence Enabled Food Recognition and Associated Calorie Level Estimation System Using Deep Neural Classification Scheme
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The DNCS (Cascaded CNN-ANN) enabled Food Recognition (FR) and Associated Calorie Level Estimation System presents a novel approach to food classification and calorie estimation using a cascaded neural network architecture. The system combines Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) for food image recognition with Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) for calorie estimation, leveraging fine-tuned pre-trained models such as InceptionV3 and EfficientNet. The system demonstrated high FR accuracy across various datasets, achieving a peak accuracy of 96.2% for common food items like burgers and pizzas, with an overall accuracy range between 89.2% and 96.2%. For calorie estimation, the system achieved a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of less than 6.1%, demonstrating reliability in predicting calorie content based on food portion size. The use of image segmentation techniques like graph-cut and GrabCut further enhanced the accuracy of FR. The system was tested for real-time applications, achieving an average processing time of 350 to 450 milliseconds per image, making it suitable for integration into mobile applications. User feedback highlighted ease of use, speed, and accuracy as key strengths, with an overall satisfaction rating of 4.7 out of 5. These results suggest that the DNCS system offers an efficient solution for dietary management through real-time calorie tracking.

articleTitle: Internet of Things Based Identification of Fault in Back Channel Cable
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The utilization of underground cables has become prevalent with the advancement of the power system grid. These cables are susceptible to various faults caused by underground conditions, deterioration, and rodent activity. Identifying the source of a fault poses a challenge, as it often necessitates excavating the entire line to inspect the cable. However, skilled repair personnel can accurately pinpoint the faulty section, allowing for targeted excavation to locate the fault source. This approach significantly conserves time and resources, facilitating quicker maintenance of underground cable systems. The objective of this project is to ascertain the distance of the underground cable fault from the base station in kilometres. The suggested method minimizes service disruptions, lowers operating expenses, and increases the accuracy of defect detection. By integrating IoT technology, it is possible to maintain a more responsive and resilient power infrastructure through continuous monitoring and real-time data processing. This study opens the door for more advancement in the field of power system management and shows how the Internet of Things has the ability to completely transform conventional fault detection techniques.

articleTitle: Integrating Machine Learning and Epidemiological Data to Forecast Zoonotic Disease Outbreaks from Avian Influenza and Other Animal
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: There are growing concerns about zoonotic diseases, such as avian influenza and other zoonotic pathogens, that increasingly threaten global health security. Advanced methods for predicting outbreaks are thus needed. This article pools epidemiological data with machine learning in order to develop a time series forecasting model capable of predicting the potential of new outbreaks using historical information. Analyses of past outbreaks, pathogen strains, geographic patterns, and temporal tr capture these relations and allow for early warnings of future zoonotic spill overs. Yet another important advantage for using machine learning in time-series analysis is that it can more effectively process complex high-dimensional data, and it might just be the key to finding some of these hidden patterns. In this way, the tools for dynamic and accurate outbreak prediction will be met, given how unpredictable and ever more frequent zoonotic diseases have become. It would be able to empower public health authorities better to foresee the outbreak potential, allocate appropriate resources beforehand, prepare relevant preventive measures, and mitigate more significant risks of transmission among the whole population. Second, this framework can be used to predict all other zoonotic diseases, including further enhancement of global public health surveillance and pandemic preparedness efforts

articleTitle: An Efficient Technique for Feature Selection in Learning to Rank Using NSGA-II
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Feature Selection (FS) is essential for optimizing Learning to Rank (LTR) models by determining the vital choice of attributes from a complex dataset. This study examines feature selection strategies within the framework of learning to rank, specifically emphasizing a multi-objective evolutionary algorithm utilizing the listwise approach. Conventional ranking algorithms frequently experience issues with superfluous or unnecessary features, undermining their efficacy. The suggested method employs a combination of instance selection, evolutionary optimization, and ensemble techniques to choose feature subsets. The methodology seeks to reduce the feature count while enhancing ranking precision, assessed via the Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain (NDCG) metric. Experiments were performed using LETOR 4.0 dataset (MQ2007-list and MQ2008-list), evaluating proposed method against established listwise ranking algorithms like ListMLE, ListNet, RankCosine and p-ListMLE. The findings indicate that, although there are performance discrepancies relative to current algorithms, the suggested method attains substantial feature reduction up to 60 percent while maintaining competitive ranking accuracy.

articleTitle: A Smart Battery Management System (BMS) Development for Electric Vehicles to Improve Energy and Power Management Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The development of a Smart Battery Management System (BMS) for electric vehicles (EVs) focuses on enhancing energy and power management by ensuring accurate State of Charge (SOC) estimation, efficient temperature control, voltage balancing, and optimized charging/discharging processes. This study implemented real-time monitoring and predictive algorithms, including neural networks optimized with genetic algorithms, to improve the accuracy of SOC estimation. The results indicated that the SOC estimation had a minimal error of 0.5% or less, with the predicted SOC closely aligning with actual values across different test scenarios. The system also effectively managed temperature, maintaining battery pack temperatures below <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$52^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> under high loads. Voltage balancing reduced discrepancies between cells, achieving a final voltage difference of less than 0.01V. Charging and discharging efficiency remained high, with an energy efficiency of 95% at lower loads and 85% at higher loads. These findings demonstrate the potential of the Smart BMS to significantly enhance the performance, safety, and lifespan of EV batteries. The system's integration of advanced algorithms and real-time data processing paves the way for more efficient battery management in EVs, making it a critical component for future sustainable transportation.

articleTitle: An Image Oriented AI Methodology to Detect Animal Footprints Based on Enhanced Neural Optimization and Classification Scheme
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The identification and detection of animal footprints are essential for the conservation of wildlife, ecological studies, and wildlife monitoring. This paper introduces a novel method for detecting animal footprints that combines deep learning and image processing. The approach, known as the Enhanced Neural Optimization and Classification Scheme (ENOCS), is cross-validated with the conventional model, the Support Vector Machine (SVM), to assess the efficacy of the proposed scheme. Our approach employs a learning model that has been fined-tuned on a dataset of various types of animal print to extract and classify features with high accuracy. The quality of the input data is enhanced through the image-processing component by eliminating noise, normalizing illumination, and performing morphological operations to draw emphasis to footprint patterns. Performance metrics are tested on a benchmark dataset containing a wide range of animal traces and evaluated with conventional image recognition methods. The results indicate that our method attains significant improvement in accuracy relative to the state-of-the-art technique, known as SVM. Furthermore, our approach is invariant to variations in environmental conditions and image quality. The proposed scheme thus provides a reliable and effective tool to identify animal imprints, thereby increasing the effectiveness of measures for ecosystems and conservation.

articleTitle: Plant Disease Detection and Classification Using Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Agriculture is a fundamental component of human civilization. It contributes to the economy while also providing sustenance. Plant foliage or crops are susceptible to many illnesses during agricultural agriculture. The illnesses impede the development of their respective species. Timely and accurate identification and categorization of illnesses may mitigate the risk of further harm to the plants. The identification and categorization of these disorders have emerged as significant challenges. The conventional methods used by farmers to forecast and identify plant leaf diseases may be tedious and inaccurate. Challenges may occur while endeavoring to manually forecast illness kinds. The failure to promptly identify and categorize plant diseases may lead to the devastation of crops, causing a substantial reduction in yield. Farmers using automated image processing techniques in their fields may mitigate losses and enhance productivity. This study proposes using a deep learning framework utilizing the latest convolutional neural network model EfficientNet to identify tomato illnesses based on 18,161 plain and segmented photos of tomato leaves. The efficacy of two segmentation theories, namely U-net and Modified U-net, for leaf segmentation is shown. The proposed methodology for plant disease identification is straightforward and computationally efficient, necessitating less time for predictions compared to previous deep learning methodologies. This document presents the computed accuracies for several plant and leaf diseases.

articleTitle: An Efficient Framework Classification for Diabetic Retinopathy Using MobileNetV2
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Diabetes is a disorder marked by unregulated glucose levels in the body, potentially causing retinal damage and leading to irreversible visual impairment or loss. Diabetes affects the eyes, resulting in diabetic retinopathy, a prevalent medical disorder, especially among the elderly. Consequently, timely and precise diabetic retinopathy screening is essential for disease prediction. Nonetheless, conventional manual detection is labor-intensive and often results in misdiagnosis for several individuals. In this study, we devised a deep learning (DL) model using transfer learning from the MobileNetV2 architecture, accompanied with an innovative color version preprocessing approach. It decreased the training duration and achieved an average accuracy of 0.93 when applied to the new Kaggle dataset “APTOS 2019 Blindness Detection.” Furthermore, to mitigate the issue of overfitting in the long term, we used Stratified K-fold cross-validation.

articleTitle: Design of Smart Water Management System for Gardens Using Arduino
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Watering serves asthe most labor-intensive task and most vital practice in day-to-day agricultural or gardening operations. The quantity of water that penetrates thecrops should be under our control, no matter what the weather conditions, being it exceptionallyhumid and waterless or excessively hazy and drenched. When such crops require watering, modern irrigation systems might be an efficient way to provide it. However, there are two crucial factors to think about when watering the crops manually: the amount and the timing of the irrigation. We have proposed an automated plant watering system using ATmega328microcontrollerto replace manual tasks and ease the workload of gardeners. All of the crops in the garden or agricultural field can grow to their full capacity by setting up a smart mechanism which can irrigate the greenery cropsand also assist to preserve water. We've developed an approach which can work flawlessly with any kind of crop in the garden, whether it is a mixture of drip irrigation micro emitter and sprayer. Sprinkler systems, pipelines, and nozzles have all been utilized in combination to build a self-operatingcrop watering system. The technique is intended to identify the plants' moisture content at the moment. Water is applied in the required amount until the moisture content falls below a predefined threshold, which is set according to the water requirements of a specific plant. Plants often require morning and evening watering twice a day. To water plants twice a day, here is how the microcontroller is configured. In addition to alerting the user when there is more water in the tank, the system is made to notify its present conditionthrough smart phone applications. Hopefully, this prototype will allow everyone to enjoy growing plants without worrying about being forgetful or absent.

articleTitle: Enhancing Email Security Using Behavior Based Authentication Method with Encrypted Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: One easy biometric approach that has shown to accurately differentiate persons is keystroke-dynamics based authentication. In this section, you will design and implement an easy-to-understand protocol that verifies the identity of computer users by tracking their keystrokes. Keystroke verification approaches might be either static or continuous. Certain parts of keystroke verification, such as the login process, are the only parts that static verification approaches look at. While static methods provide better user verification than simple passwords, they aren't able to provide continuous security as they can't detect user substitutions after the first verification. Continuous verification, in contrast, monitors the user's keystroke patterns in real time. We can build a mechanism for the mail app to store their information, including login credentials, in this project. When you type in a password, it keeps track of how long it takes to type the entire password as well as how long it takes to type each individual letter. This makes it hard for hackers to steal information. In addition, suggest using AES as an end-to-end encryption solution for email. The publicly accessible data does not need to be altered in order for these methods to work. Also, make sure that shared email accounts use one-time password authentication. Our chances of finding the responsible party and exposing leaks would be enhanced if this were to happen. There would be no use in entrusting agents with confidential information if doing so may lead to their accidental or malicious disclosure. Plus, incorporate a secret key exchange mechanism within the suggested task in case we are need to divulge sensitive information. The shared mail information will only be accessible when the key has been validated. By doing so, we can protect our email data from prying eyes.

articleTitle: LBCM: A Robust Image Based Driver Drowsiness Detection Approach Using Learning Based Blink Classification Methodology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Driver drowsiness is a significant contributor to road accidents, causing numerous fatalities and injuries each year. This paper presents the Learning-based Blink Classification Methodology (LBCM), a robust image-based approach for detecting driver drowsiness using blink classification and eye movement analysis. The system leverages real-time video input to detect facial landmarks, compute the Eye Aspect Ratio (EAR), and classify blinks into alert, drowsy, and asleep states. Using a hybrid method combining Haar Cascade and deep learning-based face detection, the system achieves accurate blink detection across varying lighting conditions. Blink classification is performed using Support Vector Machines (SVM) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), achieving a precision of 96.5% for alert states, 93.2% for drowsy states, and 90.5% for asleep states. The system's overall blink detection accuracy in real-time is above 94<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> across different driving environments, including low-light and overexposed conditions. Additionally, the system performs efficiently with a frame rate of 50–60 FPS when utilizing GPU acceleration.

articleTitle: Implementation of PV Based Converter Control for Plug-In Hybrid Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Pollution is one of the major problems in our environment. With the aim of achieving a pollution-free environment, the world has already started running beyond E-items. One such thing which does a great part in making the environment pollution free is the emergence of electric vehicles. The increasing prevalence of electric vehicles is straining the power grid, prompting the adoption of photovoltaic (PV) charging solutions to alleviate peak demand and reduce dependence on non-renewable energy sources. Thus, solar power efficiently replaces the diminishing non- renewable resources. Therefore, solar power system for plug-in electric vehicle is preferred. This paper explores the different modes of charging the Plug-in electric vehicle using both solar energy and an external battery source. It also analyses the variation of change in voltage and power due to change in irradiation. Notable advantages are achieved such as low cost, increased efficiency of the grid and eco-friendly environment. In this paper, circuit representations of individual converters, their simulations and outputs are discussed.

articleTitle: Experimental Evaluation of AI Powered Vehicle Toll Collection System Based on RFID and Internet of Things (IoT) Assistance
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This paper presents the experimental evaluation of an AI-powered vehicle toll collection system, utilizing RFID technology and IoT integration. The system was designed to automate toll collection, reducing transaction time and improving accuracy while minimizing human intervention. The methodology involved RFID-based vehicle identification, real-time data transfer via IoT, and automatic toll deductions from prepaid accounts. The system was evaluated based on transaction speed, accuracy, user satisfaction, and system reliability. Results show that the automated system significantly reduced average transaction times from 32.5 seconds (manual) to 10 seconds (automated) during peak hours. Additionally, the system demonstrated a 100% accuracy rate in detecting unregistered vehicles and low-balance scenarios. User satisfaction was high, with an average rating of 4.6 out of 5. System reliability was also excellent, achieving an average uptime of 99.5% across multiple toll booth locations. The AI-powered toll collection system proved to be highly efficient in automating toll processes, reducing congestion, and improving the user experience. These findings suggest that such systems can effectively modernize toll management, contributing to time savings, reduced operational costs, and enhanced security.

articleTitle: Hybrid Electric Vehicles with Multiple Charging System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: In India, the escalating use of two-wheelers is contributing significantly to environmental pollution due to the reliance on internal combustion (IC) engine vehicles. To mitigate pollution and reduce fuel consumption, hybrid vehicles that utilize both IC engines and batteries have been developed. These vehicles typically rely on charging stations, leading to increased electricity costs for users. To address this issue, implementing hybrid and multiple charging methods can help lower electricity expenses and decrease carbon emissions. Utilizing solar energy for driving vehicles presents a viable solution to reduce pollution and meet energy demands. This paper proposes an innovative approach to automotive design, focusing on a vehicle powered by solar energy to tackle everyday challenges. A modified 65.5cc TVS Excel equipped with a hub motor and four 12V batteries provides backup power for the bike's operation. The integration of regenerative braking technology allows for battery recharging during braking, enhancing overall efficiency and reducing energy consumption. The hub motor offers a compact and efficient electric propulsion system, improving vehicle performance and minimizing maintenance needs. This proposed hybrid electric vehicle represents a sustainable and eco-friendly transportation solution, particularly suited for urban environments.

articleTitle: Health Data Analytics Using IoT: Transforming Healthcare Management and Treatment Strategies for Improved Patient Outcomes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The integration of Web of Things (IoT) innovation within the healthcare segment has revolutionized conventional healthcare administration and treatment procedures, driving progressed quiet results. This paper looks at the transformative effect of well-being information analytics utilizing IoT in upgrading healthcare administrations, optimizing understanding care, and advancing preventive measures. The paper analyzes the key components and applications of IoT in healthcare, emphasizing its part in information collection, real-time observation, and examination of understanding imperative signs, action levels, and pharmaceutical adherence. With the help of IoT-enabled gadgets such as wearables, sensors, and keen checking frameworks, healthcare experts can assemble comprehensive, real-time persistent information, encouraging early discovery and opportune mediation for basic well-being issues. Besides, the utilization of IoT in well-being information analytics empowers the improvement of personalized treatment plans custom-fitted to a person's persistent needs, cultivating a patient-centric approach to healthcare conveyance. By leveraging machine learning calculations and prescient analytics, healthcare suppliers can expect potential well-being complications, in this manner minimizing the chance of antagonistic occasions and clinic readmissions. In addition, the execution of IoT-based healthcare arrangements advances further understanding and observing, empowering healthcare suppliers to offer ceaseless, personalized care past conventional healthcare settings.

articleTitle: Classification of UAV Images into Flood / Non-Flood Region Using Deep-Transfer-Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The Deep-Learning (DL) tool based schemes are widely employed in a variety of image examination tasks to find the solution for a chosen problem. Examination of grey-scale image and the RGB-scale image is commonly performed using the chosen DL-models. The DL-based methods are commonly employed to analyze the environmental data for alerting the people when the environmental condition becomes abnormal. This work aims to develop a DL-based scheme to examine the flood/non-flood images to accurately detect the flood and alert the people during the abnormal situations. This research considered the ResNet (RN) scheme based approach to detect the flood from the chosen image database. The different phases in this scheme includes; image collection and resizing, feature extraction with the chosen RN-model, feature based classification using SoftMax (SM), and performance verification using three-fold cross-validation. This study considered various RN-models with variants, like 50, 101, and 152 and the outcome of this study confirmed that the RN101 with integrated features with RNV2101 provided a better detection accuracy of >96%. This confirms that the proposed scheme works well on this database.

articleTitle: Fruit Insight - Deep Learning-Based 2D Image Analysis for Evaluating Fruit Quality and Freshness
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The detection of calcium carbide in those artificially ripened bananas and an in-depth analysis of fruit, quality, freshness, nutritional values. First, these 2D images of the fruit are run through CNNs which train the model to turn it into things that are of interest, the color, texture and shape properties. Obviously, the levels of accuracy required by the model necessitate pre-processing techniques such as scaling, normalization, and augmentation. It is the same CNN model but through feature extraction and ROI segmentation it recognizes the signs of artificial ripening. Also, an MLP is applied to the regression problem of predicting the chemical and nutritional content of the fruit from the attributes obtained from the CNN as well as additional relevant information. Through the process of categorization and suggesting what to eat and what not to eat (as far as health goes) this approach uses the VGG16 model to recognize the harmful substances from calcium carbide ripening. Not only does this product offer consumer nutrition information that would hopefully encourage them to make a healthier food choice, but this product is a completely automated system that uses real-time data and a scale to ensure food safety based on the knowledge that many ripening practices are hazardous. The system is rated based on its accuracy, precision and RMSE. It works in real time using TensorFlow Serving or TorchServe.

articleTitle: LDCP: A Novel Approach to Predict Fake Reviews in Online Social Network by using Learning based Data Classification Principle
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The proliferation of online reviews has significantly impacted consumer decision-making processes, making the detection of fake reviews crucial for maintaining trust in e-commerce platforms. This study presents a novel approach for detecting fake reviews using machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) models, with a focus on achieving high accuracy through advanced feature extraction techniques and data augmentation. Various models, including classical ML algorithms such as Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Random Forest, alongside DL models like Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM), and Cascaded Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), were evaluated. Feature extraction methods like TF-IDF, GloVe, and combined approaches were used to enhance performance. The DL model RoBERTa achieved the highest accuracy of 99.5%, while Cascaded MLP reached 99.2%. Classical models like Random Forest and SVM also performed well, achieving accuracies of 97.1 % and 96.8%, respectively. Data augmentation techniques, such as back-translation, further improved the models' ability to handle imbalanced datasets. The results demonstrate that combining DL architectures with advanced feature extraction leads to superior performance in fake review detection.

articleTitle: Design of a Highly Isolated Compact Quad Port Orthogonal MIMO Antenna with DGS for C and X band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: In this paper a low profile, miniaturized4-port MIMO antenna with DGS for dual band applications is presented. The suggested MIMO antenna design is a compact form, measuring 60×60×1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, belies the sophistication within, where each parameter, meticulously set, contributes to its exceptional functionality. Noteworthy among its design features is the ingenious use of the stub method, which achieves remarkable isolation enhancements of up to 20dB across a broad operational bandwidth spanning from 6 GHz to 18 GHz. Central to its design ethos is the strategic integration of advanced isolation techniques, prominently featuring Defected Ground Structures (DGS) with rectangular patch antenna. As this proposed MIMO antenna has a 20dB average isolation, S11 >-25 dB. The proposed antenna's diversity performance characteristics are investigated, and the obtained values are 0.00001 and 0.00009, approximately 10dB, ±3dB for 6.96GHz and 10.52Ghz respectively. This proposed antenna system emerges as a beacon of innovation, poised to address the multifaceted encounters and opportunities presented by the dynamic landscape of modern wireless communication.

articleTitle: Streamlined Ayurvedic Species Detection Using VGG16 and Neural Networks Chatbot Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: In response to the growing need for enhanced medicinal herbs for various diseases and medicines have a vital role in in maintaining both the physical and psychological well-being of individuals The proper identification and categorization of plants with medicinal properties are essential for better treatment. The medical Plant Classification System presented in this project addresses the need for an efficient and accurate method of identifying and categorizing medicinal plants within the context of Ayurvedic medicine. Leveraging advanced machine learning techniques, specifically convolutional neural networks (CNNs), the system employs a robust model trained on a diverse dataset of medicinal plants. Furthermore, a chatbot component using NLP technology, interacts with users to provide information about the varied realm of medicinal plants. This chatbot feature, driven by NLP algorithms, facilitates dialogue and offers knowledge on the diverse world of plants used for medicinal purposes.

articleTitle: IoT and Cybersecurity Regulations: Compliance and Risk Management Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Within the scope of this investigation paper, the vital intersection of cybersecurity rules and the Internet of Things (IoT) is investigated, with a particular emphasis placed on compliance and threat operation tactics. Businesses have become more concerned about their susceptibility to cyber threats as the Internet of Things (IoT) bias has spread across a variety of fields. This has led to an increase in the number of nonsupervisory interventions that are targeted at safeguarding data sequestration and security. This paper elucidates the geography of Internet of Things cybersecurity regulations by conducting a comprehensive review of existing literature and nonsupervisory fabrics. In a similar vein, the article investigates the difficulties that associations encounter when attempting to adhere to these requirements and outlines effective threat operation tactics that can help mitigate the cybersecurity risks that are connected with Internet of Things deployments. This paper aims to assist policymakers, diligent interpreters, and cybersecurity professionals in navigating the complex terrain of Internet of Things (IoT) cybersecurity regulations and enhancing the adaptability of IoT ecosystems against cyber pitfalls. This will be accomplished by providing insight into nonsupervisory compliance conditions and threat mitigation approaches.

articleTitle: ThermoShield: An IoT Arduino-Based Cooling and Heat Sensor Monitoring System with Weather Forecasting and Advisory Using Linear Regression for Enhanced Mobile Phone Protection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Mobile phones are essential tools for productivity and daily activities but are vulnerable to overheating, particularly in high-temperature environments. This can result in hardware damage, data loss, and potential safety hazards, especially in tropical regions where extreme heat is prevalent. To mitigate these issues, the researchers propose an IoT-based, Arduino-powered cooling and heat monitoring system that regulates device temperature and provides real-time monitoring within a protective casing. The system also integrates weather forecasting and advisory recommendations using linear regression to optimize cooling mechanisms. This solution aims to enhance mobile phone protection and user satisfaction, making it ideal for individuals frequently exposed to high temperatures. The system was evaluated using International Organization for Standardization (ISO) 25010 software quality standards and achieved mean scores of 3.51 for Functional Suitability, 3.50 for Reliability, and 3.62 for Portability—each classified as “Very Satisfied”. The mobile application successfully integrated weather forecasting using a linear regression model; however, its performance is constrained by limited access to weather data specific to the Philippines. Future enhancements will focus on improving data access and more opportunities in accessing weather data. Evaluation results demonstrated positive feedback across all categories, confirming the system's effectiveness and functionality in meeting its intended purpose.

articleTitle: CNOL: An Efficient Red Blood Cell Smears Based Malaria Disease Detection Using Digital Image Processing Technique with Convoluted Neural Optimization Logic
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Malaria is a life-threatening disease affecting millions worldwide, and early diagnosis is critical for effective treatment. This study proposes CNOL (Convoluted Neural Optimization Logic), an efficient system for detecting malaria from red blood cell (RBC) smear images using digital image processing and neural network optimization. The CNOL model employs a convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture optimized through an advanced neural logic framework, enhancing its ability to classify infected and non-infected RBCs. A diverse dataset of blood smear images is processed through techniques such as image normalization, segmentation, and feature extraction to prepare data for model training. The model achieved a remarkable accuracy of 97.2%, with high precision (95.8%) and recall (96.9%), outperforming several existing methods like traditional CNNs, SVMs, and KNNs. The CNOL model demonstrated robust performance across all evaluation metrics, including a high AUC-ROC score of 98.1%, indicating its strong discriminatory ability. The model's time and resource efficiency make it suitable for real-time clinical use, requiring minimal computational power while providing accurate and timely diagnoses.

articleTitle: Enhancing Thermal Object Detection in Adverse Weather Conditions for Automotive Applications Using Deep Learning-Based CNN and SVM Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Northeastern Indian cities Such as Delhi have harsh weather conditions, and high air pollution often results in poor visibility, leading to numerous accidents. This paper proposes a thermal object detection system that leverages thermal imaging and deep learning algorithms to detect vehicles and objects based on their heat signatures to address this issue. Unlike traditional vision-based systems that rely on visible light, this approach is resilient to low-light conditions, shadows, and glare, ensuring reliable detection even in challenging environments. The system is tested on real-world images, demonstrating its effectiveness in traffic management, security, and industrial automation. Additionally, thermal imaging technology provides advantages such as detecting objects at longer ranges and offering insights into temperature and material properties. These findings show the potential to significantly enhance safety and security in scenarios where visibility is compromised.

articleTitle: Utilizing Deep Learning in Smart Cities for Environmental Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The effectiveness and dependability of services provided by smart cities are significantly impacted by the significant and difficult issue of intrusion detection. Replay attacks, which weaken security via improper authentication in a smart city network, are among the most common threats to this infrastructure. For example, replay attacks have the potential to severely damage the smart city structure, leading to the loss of crucial data and substantial monetary losses. As a result, we have developed a model based on deep learning to predict where attacks in smart cities would be replayed. The proposed approach is intriguing since it uses deep learning-based models as an application to differentiate replay assaults and increase recognition accuracy. Replay attacks are simulated on a real-world smart city dataset, and the model's performance is assessed by using this dataset. Our findings demonstrate that the suggested model may reasonably accurately discriminate between normal and assault actions. Furthermore, our suggested model performs better than both deep learning and conventional classification models, per the findings.

articleTitle: Automated Medicinal Plant Recognition Using Capsule Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Medicinal plants are necessary for traditional as well as modern medicine, offering natural medication for a wide range of conditions. Accurate classification of these plants is essential to ensure their correct identification, which is crucial for safe usage, drug development, and conservation efforts. Misidentification can lead to ineffective treatment or even harmful effects. Additionally, proper classification aids in preserving biodiversity, supporting sustainable use, and protecting endangered species. The proposed system offers an innovative approach to medicinal plant identification by integrating Capsule Networks and the YOLO algorithm, addressing the critical need for accuracy in traditional medicine, conservation, and pharmacology. Manual identification is labor-intensive and error-prone, driving the development of automated systems. Conventional CNNs, while effective in classification, struggle with generalization and feature learning, and YOLO's use of rectangular bounding boxes can limit its accuracy in capturing complex leaf shapes. Capsule Networks maintain spatial hierarchies and handle affine transformations, enhancing feature extraction, while YOLO ensures real-time detection and accurate localization. The system was trained on a massive dataset of medicinal plant pictures, using upscaling and normalization techniques to improve precision. By leveraging the strengths of both Capsule Networks and YOLO, the architecture achieves superior performance, making it suitable for practical applications, including mobile devices.

articleTitle: Evaluating Advertisement Appeals' Effectiveness on Top of Mind Awareness Using AI and Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The purpose of this research is to evaluate the effectiveness of a variety of marketing strategies in influencing consumers' Top of Mind Awareness (TOMA) by utilising AI and machine learning technology. TOMA is a valuable indicator for brand managers to employ, as it represents the brand that people predominantly connect with a particular category. For an extended period, surveys and focus groups have been frequently employed to evaluate the efficacy of advertisements, despite their potential for bias and time-consuming nature. This research employs sophisticated artificial intelligence and machine learning algorithms to analyse digital footprints, including search engine queries and social media participation, in order to determine the most effective advertising concepts for enhancing TOMA (top-of-mind awareness). The study utilises natural language processing (NLP) to analyse customer sentiment and the relationship between keywords, utilising machine learning algorithms to predict and evaluate the efficacy of various advertising strategies. Marketers can derive significant value from the findings, as they can determine which appeals are most likely to increase top-of-mind awareness (TOMA) among their target audience. This, in turn, allows them to create advertising campaigns that are more effective.

articleTitle: Empirical Development of a Novel Solar Powered Electric Vehicles (EVs) Charging Station to Avoid Environmental Pollution
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The development of solar-powered electric vehicle (EV) charging stations offers an environmentally friendly and cost-effective solution to address the increasing demand for renewable energy in the transportation sector. This study focuses on designing, implementing, and evaluating a novel solar-powered EV charging station to reduce dependency on fossil fuels and minimize CO2 emissions. The system included solar panels, energy storage, and efficient power management technologies. Tests showed that the station achieved an energy generation efficiency of 95% under optimal sunny conditions, with an average charging efficiency of 94.5% across different EV models. In comparison with grid-based charging, solar charging significantly reduced costs, with monthly grid charging costs amounting to $362.5, while solar charging incurred zero costs. Additionally, solar charging eliminated 1,448 kg of CO2 emissions annually per vehicle. These results demonstrate that solar-powered charging stations are not only feasible but also highly effective in reducing environmental impact and operating expenses. The prototype's ability to maintain consistent performance under varying weather conditions highlights its potential for widespread adoption.

articleTitle: TailorAIDE: A Regression Analysis-Based System for Predicting Cost Estimation in the Clothing Industry
